title: Playing a dance in a dairy barn
summary: His Gentilly pickup band got stuck in mud and played for dancers in a barn full of cows.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Well to get back to the early days, you told me you played with this guy Stevens, Ernest Stevens, and you played some other little jobs. Do you remember the names of the other bands you worked with, Ernest Stevens?

There were so many. There was a little pickup band I used to play with, fellas back in Gentilly. Now that section's all paved now, but in those days it was mud streets, mud roads, and we went to a job one night on Frenchman near Gentilly Boulevard, and we got stuck in the mud there. It was a T-model Ford. I mean, you just couldn't get through. We had to walk the last way to the—and the thing was given in a barn. A dairy. A dairy barn full of cows. And we played—we played for a dance in the thing on the mud floor. People were dancing right on the mud.
Did the cows like the music?
Well, they didn't seem to mind it. I mean, they didn't do anything about it. They just stayed in their stalls while we played our jazz, you know.

One time I was following a colored parade in Marrero, you know, the jazz band. And they passed the dairy farm and the cows followed the band. They must have liked it. Must have influenced them some kind of way. And they would dance along, you know. That was funny. Fortunately, there's a movie of that. A friend of mine made a movie of that. You'd have to see the movie to believe it. I could imagine. That's pretty fantastic.
